decks.name: KNM - Kennis van de Nederlandse Maatschappij (v2, cleaned)
decks.description:
One fact per card, or a closed set of at most five with the count stated in the front.

Bron: Bijlage 2 bij artikel 3.2, Regeling inburgering 2021 (Stcrt. 2024, nr. 15802), van kracht sinds 2025-07-01.

Bouwregels:
• One fact per card, or a closed set of at most five with the expected count stated in the front.
• No yes/no fronts whose answer is guessable; inverted to which/what/who/how many.
• No meta-fronts ('what must you know about X').
• Every front answerable standalone, independent of neighbouring cards.
• Regional, procedural and read-once material moved out of the drill deck to preserve eindterm coverage without polluting the review queue.

cards.front: Which module prepares an inburgeraar for the labour market?
cards.back: The Module Arbeidsmarkt en Participatie (MAP).

cards.front: Who is expected to provide your income in the Netherlands?
cards.back: You are - there is an obligation to make an effort to earn your own income.

cards.front: Besides your own network, where are Dutch vacancies mainly advertised?
cards.back: In online vacaturebanken.

cards.front: What is an uitzendbureau?
cards.back: A temp agency: you register with it and it places you in work.

cards.front: Name the three documents used to apply for Dutch jobs.
cards.back: An application form, a sollicitatiebrief, and a CV.

cards.front: What do Dutch employers expect a candidate to do at interview?
cards.back: Arrive prepared, and ask a few questions about the work and the terms.

cards.front: Name all five factors that determine your Dutch labour-market chances.
cards.back: Prior education, work experience, availability, motivation, command of Dutch.

cards.front: Which service assesses the value of a foreign diploma?
cards.back: IDW - Internationale Diplomawaardering, run by Nuffic for higher education and SBB for mbo.

cards.front: Which two competences may an employer set requirements on?
cards.back: Language and communication skills.

cards.front: You lose a job you had worked in. Which body do you register with?
cards.back: UWV.

cards.front: You need income support and have no Dutch work history. Which body?
cards.back: The gemeente.

cards.front: Which benefit is the minimum-income safety net?
cards.back: Bijstand.

cards.front: Which benefit follows the loss of a job you had worked in?
cards.back: WW.

cards.front: Which benefit covers inability to work through illness or disability?
cards.back: Arbeidsongeschiktheidsuitkering.

cards.front: What obligation does a benefit recipient have towards offered work?
cards.back: To accept it, in principle.

cards.front: What must you report to the benefits body when circumstances change?
cards.back: Any change in your income situation - it can affect the benefit.

cards.front: What is a cao?
cards.back: A collectieve arbeidsovereenkomst - a sector-wide collective agreement on employment terms.

cards.front: If a cao covers your sector, what can you still do?
cards.back: Negotiate your terms with the employer independently of it.

cards.front: What is a beoordelingsgesprek?
cards.back: A performance review of how you are functioning.

cards.front: Name the three types of employment contract.
cards.back: Permanent (vast), fixed-term (tijdelijk), and via an uitzendbureau.

cards.front: Name five things an arbeidsovereenkomst regulates.
cards.back: Any five of: hours, salary, autonomy, communication, working conditions, safety, environment, leave, sickness.

cards.front: Which working pattern is unusually common in the Netherlands?
cards.back: Part-time work (deeltijd).

cards.front: What is the ondernemingsraad?
cards.back: The works council - a statutory form of employee participation.

cards.front: What is a personeelsvereniging?
cards.back: A staff association.

cards.front: Name the two functions of a vakbond.
cards.back: Defending workers' rights and interests, and concluding cao's.

cards.front: Who withholds your taxes and social premiums?
cards.back: Your employer, from your salary.

cards.front: Besides the employer, who is bound by the ban on workplace discrimination?
cards.back: Colleagues.

cards.front: Name three places to turn if you suspect discrimination at work.
cards.back: A vertrouwenspersoon, a trade union, an equal-rights organisation.

cards.front: What registration is compulsory to start a business?
cards.back: Registration with the Kamer van Koophandel (KvK).

cards.front: What happens to your benefit when you register with the KvK?
cards.back: It lapses in principle - consult the benefits body or gemeente first.

cards.front: Which two things must a self-employed person arrange themselves?
cards.back: A supplementary pension, and disability insurance.

cards.front: What is expected before visiting an office or service provider?
cards.back: Making an appointment in advance.

sources.title: Thema 2 (Omgangsvormen, waarden en normen) — eindterm 2.1.3 · regulation

cards.front: Name the two things many Dutch people expect around appointments.
cards.back: Punctuality, and cancelling in good time.

sources.title: Thema 2 (Omgangsvormen, waarden en normen) — eindterm 2.1.3 · regulation

cards.front: Which two partnership forms are regulated by Dutch law?
cards.back: Marriage (huwelijk) and registered partnership (geregistreerd partnerschap).

sources.title: Thema 2 (Omgangsvormen, waarden en normen) — eindterm 2.1.4 · regulation

cards.front: Which partnership forms are open to same-sex couples in NL?
cards.back: Both marriage and registered partnership.

sources.title: Thema 2 (Omgangsvormen, waarden en normen) — eindterm 2.1.4 · regulation

cards.front: What is commemorated on 4 May?
cards.back: Nationale Dodenherdenking - the war dead.

sources.title: Thema 2 (Omgangsvormen, waarden en normen) — eindterm 2.1.5 · regulation

cards.front: What is celebrated on 5 May?
cards.back: Bevrijdingsdag - the liberation of 1945.

sources.title: Thema 2 (Omgangsvormen, waarden en normen) — eindterm 2.1.5 · regulation

cards.front: Which national holiday celebrates the monarch?
cards.back: Koningsdag.

sources.title: Thema 2 (Omgangsvormen, waarden en normen) — eindterm 2.1.5 · regulation

cards.front: Name the four festivals the eindtermen list as relevant in particular circles.
cards.back: Sinterklaas, Carnival, Suikerfeest, Keti Koti.

sources.title: Thema 2 (Omgangsvormen, waarden en normen) — eindterm 2.1.5 · regulation

cards.front: How do the eindtermen say you build a social network?
cards.back: Through volunteering, and active involvement in clubs and associations.

sources.title: Thema 2 (Omgangsvormen, waarden en normen) — eindterm 2.2.1 · regulation

cards.front: What is a huurcontract?
cards.back: A rental contract setting out the terms of the tenancy.

cards.front: Which body rules on disputes over rent, service charges and maintenance?
cards.back: The Huurcommissie.

cards.front: Where can a tenant get free legal advice?
cards.back: The Juridisch Loket.

cards.front: Name the three routes to housing in the Netherlands.
cards.back: Social rent, free-sector rent, and purchase.

cards.front: Why does registering early as a housing-seeker matter?
cards.back: Waiting time counts towards allocation in the social sector.

cards.front: What determines eligibility for sociale huur?
cards.back: An income limit, set annually.

cards.front: Who can help you find a property to rent or buy?
cards.back: A makelaar.

cards.front: Who arranges energy, water and internet connections in your home?
cards.back: You do.

cards.front: What is a meterstand and what do you do with it?
cards.back: A meter reading - you report it to the supplier when required.

cards.front: Your electricity fails. Who do you report the storing to?
cards.back: The energy supplier.

cards.front: Name the two components of an energy or water bill.
cards.back: Consumption (verbruik) and costs.

cards.front: Give the two reasons the eindtermen offer for using energy sparingly.
cards.back: It is better for the environment, and it lowers your bill.

cards.front: How does a fixed energy contract differ from a variable one?
cards.back: Fixed tariffs hold for a set term; variable tariffs can change.

cards.front: Name four ways to save energy at home.
cards.back: Any four of: lower the thermostat, draught strips, radiator foil, shorter showers, LED bulbs, avoid standby, lower wash temperature, insulation.

cards.front: Who sets the rules for waste collection and separation?
cards.back: Your gemeente.

cards.front: Why does afvalscheiding matter?
cards.back: Separated waste is recycled into new raw materials, saving energy and reducing incineration.

cards.front: Who is the first point of contact for any health problem?
cards.back: The huisarts, with the praktijkondersteuner.

cards.front: How do you gain access to a GP in the Netherlands?
cards.back: Choose a practice and register with it.

cards.front: How do you see your GP?
cards.back: By appointment.

cards.front: What right do you have if you cannot follow your GP in Dutch?
cards.back: The right to a tolk.

cards.front: Where do you first go with psychological complaints?
cards.back: The huisarts or the praktijkondersteuner.

cards.front: What is the beroepsgeheim?
cards.back: Medical confidentiality - your information is passed on only with your consent.

cards.front: What do you need to collect prescription medicine at the apotheek?
cards.back: A recept.

cards.front: Where do you buy medicines that need no prescription?
cards.back: At a drogist.

cards.front: What does a mondhygienist do?
cards.back: Dental hygiene care, alongside the tandarts.

cards.front: How do you get a dentist in the Netherlands?
cards.back: Choose your own tandarts and register.

cards.front: What does kraamzorg provide?
cards.back: Maternity care in the period after birth.

cards.front: What does the consultatiebureau do?
cards.back: Monitors the health and development of young children.

cards.front: Who refers you to a specialist or to mental health care?
cards.back: The huisarts.

cards.front: Where do you go for GP care in the evening or at the weekend?
cards.back: The huisartsenpost.

cards.front: What must you do before going to the huisartsenpost?
cards.back: Telephone first - you cannot walk in.

cards.front: What number do you call in a life-threatening emergency?
Which insurance is compulsory for every resident?
cards.back: The zorgverzekering.

cards.front: How often may you change health insurer?
cards.back: Once a year.

cards.front: Name five things covered by the basispakket.
cards.back: GP care, district nursing, pregnancy and birth care, elderly care, mental health care.

cards.front: Up to what age are dental care and physiotherapy covered by the basispakket?
What is the eigen risico?
cards.back: The compulsory deductible you pay yourself before the insurer reimburses.

cards.front: Which common form of care is exempt from the eigen risico?
cards.back: GP consultations.

cards.front: What payment flexibility exists for the eigen risico?
cards.back: It may be paid in instalments.

cards.front: What does supplementary insurance cover?
cards.back: Care outside the basispakket - adult dental care, extra physiotherapy, glasses, orthodontics.

cards.front: Which digital credential do you need to arrange most care provisions?
cards.back: A DigiD.

cards.front: Where can you get help with DigiD and digital forms?
cards.back: The Informatiepunt Digitale Overheid, in public libraries.

cards.front: Name five welzijn services every gemeente provides.
cards.back: Help with debt and poverty, with social isolation, with participation, and home support for the elderly and for the chronically ill and disabled.

cards.front: What drove Dutch prosperity in the seventeenth century?
cards.back: Shipping and trade.

cards.front: Where is the seventeenth-century flowering still visible today?
cards.back: In painting and architecture.

cards.front: What do the eindtermen require you to know about the colonial period?
cards.back: The Netherlands founded colonies, enslaved and traded people, and put them to work on plantations.

cards.front: Name the four features of the Dutch tradition of managing water.
cards.back: Polders, windmills, dikes, the Deltawerken.

cards.front: What is the Dutch national anthem?
cards.back: Het Wilhelmus.

cards.front: Describe the Dutch flag.
cards.back: Three horizontal bands - red on top, then white, then blue.

cards.front: Which country occupied the Netherlands in the Second World War?
cards.back: Germany.

cards.front: What was the holocaust?
cards.back: The mass murder of Jews; many Dutch Jews were killed.

cards.front: What is the legal status of antisemitism in the Netherlands?
cards.back: Prohibited by law.

cards.front: In which year was the Netherlands liberated?
Name the three groups that immigrated to NL after the war.
cards.back: People from the former colonies, labour migrants, and refugees.

cards.front: Name the three international organisations NL joined after the war.
cards.back: The EU, NATO, and the UN.

cards.front: Name the four values many Dutch have held since the 1960s.
cards.back: Individual freedom, emancipation, tolerance, self-determination.

cards.front: Name the three rights the eindtermen list as legally established in NL.
cards.back: Abortion, same-sex marriage, euthanasia.

cards.front: What is the capital of the Netherlands?
cards.back: Amsterdam.

cards.front: Where does the Dutch government sit?
cards.back: The Hague.

cards.front: How many provinces does the Netherlands have?
cards.back: Twelve.

cards.front: Where in NL is Groningen?
cards.back: The far north-east.

cards.front: Where in NL is Friesland?
cards.back: The north-west, above the IJsselmeer.

cards.front: Where in NL is Drenthe?
cards.back: The north-east, below Groningen.

cards.front: Where in NL is Overijssel?
cards.back: The east, north of Gelderland.

cards.front: Where in NL is Flevoland?
cards.back: The centre - land reclaimed from the former Zuiderzee.

cards.front: Where in NL is Gelderland?
cards.back: The centre-east; it is the largest province by area.

cards.front: Where in NL is Utrecht?
cards.back: The centre of the country.

cards.front: Where in NL is Noord-Holland?
cards.back: The north-west coast; it contains Amsterdam.

cards.front: Where in NL is Zuid-Holland?
cards.back: The west coast; it contains The Hague and Rotterdam.

cards.front: Where in NL is Zeeland?
cards.back: The south-west - islands and peninsulas.

cards.front: Where in NL is Noord-Brabant?
cards.back: The south, along the Belgian border.

cards.front: Where in NL is Limburg?
cards.back: The south-east - a narrow strip between Belgium and Germany.

cards.front: Which two payment methods are used on Dutch public transport?
cards.back: The OV-chipkaart, and OVpay with a contactless card or phone.

cards.front: What must you do at both ends of every public-transport journey?
cards.back: Check in, and check out.

cards.front: What is the BSN?
cards.back: Burgerservicenummer - your personal number for dealings with government.

cards.front: What is DigiD used for?
cards.back: Logging in securely to Dutch government services.

cards.front: What does Nibud do?
cards.back: Provides budgeting and household-finance guidance.

cards.front: What is the Juridisch Loket?
cards.back: A service providing free legal advice.

cards.front: What does the GGD do?
cards.back: It is the municipal public health service.

cards.front: What is schuldhulpverlening?
cards.back: Assistance for people in debt.

cards.front: Which register holds your personal details at the gemeente?
cards.back: The Basisregistratie Personen (BRP).

cards.front: Name five life events you must report to the gemeente.
cards.back: Any five of: birth, marriage, cohabitation, divorce, death, moving house, migration.

cards.front: What must an unmarried father do to establish legal fatherhood?
cards.back: Register erkenning of the child.

cards.front: Why do changes in household composition matter beyond the register?
cards.back: They can affect your benefits.

cards.front: Which body issues residence permits?
cards.back: The IND.

cards.front: Which body issues your passport and ID card?
cards.back: Your gemeente.

cards.front: Which body runs driving-licence examinations?
cards.back: The CBR.

cards.front: Which body registers vehicles and driving licences?
cards.back: The RDW.

cards.front: Where do you apply for naturalisation?
cards.back: At your gemeente, which forwards the application to the IND.

cards.front: What must you normally do with your existing nationality when naturalising?
cards.back: Give it up - dual nationality is in principle not permitted.
cards.explanation: exam-convention — The exam's expected answer is simpler than the real legal position.

cards.front: Name four taxes or levies collected by the gemeente.
cards.back: OZB, rioolheffing, afvalstoffenheffing, parkeerbelasting.

cards.front: What is a jaaropgave?
cards.back: The annual statement of income from your employer.

cards.front: How does bruto differ from netto income?
cards.back: Bruto is before tax and premiums; netto is what actually reaches you.

cards.front: How long must you keep your jaaropgave?
cards.back: At least five years.

cards.front: Name five things Dutch tax money pays for.
cards.back: Education, healthcare, roads, government, and the police and judiciary.

cards.front: Who can help you file a tax return on a low income?
cards.back: The gemeente or maatschappelijk werk; unions help their members.

cards.front: Which body pays out toeslagen?
cards.back: The Belastingdienst.

cards.front: Name the three toeslagen the eindtermen list.
cards.back: Zorgtoeslag, huurtoeslag, kinderopvangtoeslag.

cards.front: How do you obtain a toeslag you are entitled to?
cards.back: Apply for it - it is not granted automatically.

cards.front: Which body pays kinderbijslag?
cards.back: The Sociale Verzekeringsbank (SVB).

cards.front: Name the three roles of the Dutch police.
cards.back: Protecting, supervising, and enforcing.

cards.front: Which crimes are you obliged to report to the police?
cards.back: Serious crimes - murder, manslaughter, rape, abduction.

cards.front: From what age must you show ID on request in public space?
From what age must you show ID on public transport?
Where do you complain about the conduct of a government body?
cards.back: The municipal ombudsman, or the Nationale ombudsman.

cards.front: What is the status of corruption by government or police?
cards.back: Prohibited and punishable.

cards.front: Name the two sources of legal help the eindtermen give.
cards.back: An advocaat, and the Juridisch Loket.

cards.front: What do you pay for subsidised legal help?
cards.back: An eigen bijdrage, scaled to your income.

cards.front: Which insurance is compulsory for motor vehicle owners?
cards.back: WA - liability insurance.

cards.front: What is the status of WA insurance for people generally?
cards.back: Not compulsory, but strongly advised.

cards.front: Which insurance must a homeowner hold?
cards.back: An opstalverzekering.

cards.front: Which tax must a vehicle owner pay?
cards.back: Motorrijtuigenbelasting.

cards.front: What is the King's function in the Dutch state?
cards.back: Chiefly ceremonial.

cards.front: Who is the King of the Netherlands?
cards.back: Willem-Alexander.
cards.explanation: volatile — Names a current officeholder; re-verify before the exam.

cards.front: Name the two chambers of the Dutch parliament.
cards.back: The Tweede Kamer and the Eerste Kamer.

cards.front: Who makes Dutch law?
cards.back: The two chambers of parliament together with the regering.

cards.front: What kind of party system does the Netherlands have?
cards.back: A multi-party system, in which parties form coalition governments.

cards.front: Name the three levels of Dutch government.
cards.back: Rijk, provincie, gemeente.

cards.front: Name three things EU membership gives citizens.
cards.back: Free movement of people and goods, free establishment in member states, and voting in European elections.

cards.front: Name the three powers of the state.
cards.back: Legislative, executive, judicial.

cards.front: What can you do if you disagree with a judge's ruling?
cards.back: Lodge an appeal - hoger beroep - though the ruling must be accepted.

cards.front: How does actief kiesrecht differ from passief kiesrecht?
cards.back: Actief is the right to vote; passief is the right to stand for election.

cards.front: In which elections may a non-Dutch resident vote?
cards.back: Municipal elections.

cards.front: How long must a non-Dutch national have lived in NL to vote municipally?
cards.back: More than five years.

cards.front: Name five kinds of Dutch election or vote.
cards.back: Municipal, provincial, Tweede Kamer, European Parliament, waterschappen.

cards.front: What does equality of women and men entail, per the eindterm?
cards.back: The same chances to develop as independent individuals, including through education and work.

cards.front: What limits freedom of expression in the Netherlands?
cards.back: The law - you may not say or write what the law prohibits.

cards.front: What must you accept about Dutch public debate?
cards.back: That some statements may be experienced as hurtful.

cards.front: What does freedom of religion cover in the Netherlands?
cards.back: Freedom to choose your own religion, philosophy of life, or ideals.

cards.front: Which prevails - the law of the state, or of religion and tradition?
cards.back: The law of the state.
cards.explanation: exam-convention — The exam's expected answer is simpler than the real legal position.

cards.front: On what condition does government stay out of a religious community's internal affairs?
cards.back: As long as the community obeys the law.

cards.front: What does Article 1 of the Grondwet establish?
cards.back: Equal treatment in equal cases, and a prohibition on discrimination.

cards.front: Name four grounds of discrimination prohibited by Article 1.
cards.back: Any four of: religion, belief, political opinion, race, sex, disability, sexual orientation.

cards.front: Where do you report discrimination?
cards.back: At a meldpunt, and at the police.

cards.front: How much personal data should you give an institution?
cards.back: Only what it needs for its task.

cards.front: Name the two rights you have over data you have shared.
cards.back: To inspect it, and to correct it where necessary.

cards.front: What does the law say about bodily integrity?
cards.back: It is protected; all unwanted intimacy and violence is punishable.

cards.front: Name the four violations of bodily integrity the eindterm lists.
cards.back: Domestic violence, honour killing, hitting children, female circumcision.

cards.front: What is the default organ-donation position in the Netherlands?
cards.back: You are a donor after death unless you register otherwise.

cards.front: How do you opt out of organ donation?
cards.back: Register that you do not wish to participate, or only in part.

cards.front: What does zelfbeschikkingsrecht mean for women in NL?
cards.back: A woman decides for herself about her own life and body - marriage, work, study, children, contraception, abortion.

cards.front: From what age do Dutch children attend primary school?
What provision exists for children with a special care requirement?
cards.back: Speciaal onderwijs.

cards.front: What may restrict moving to the next level of education?
cards.back: Toelatingseisen - admission requirements.

cards.front: What is vrijheid van onderwijs?
cards.back: The freedom to found schools on your own religious or educational basis.

cards.front: How does openbaar onderwijs differ from bijzonder onderwijs?
cards.back: Openbaar is public and non-denominational; bijzonder rests on a religious or educational vision.

cards.front: Between which ages does leerplicht run?
Between which ages does kwalificatieplicht run?
Who fixes the dates of school holidays?
cards.back: The school - and its dates are binding on parents.

cards.front: What is vve?
cards.back: Voorschoolse educatie - pre-school education for young children.

cards.front: What is bso?
cards.back: Buitenschoolse opvang - out-of-school care.

cards.front: Which allowance helps parents pay for childcare?
cards.back: Kinderopvangtoeslag.

cards.front: Which subject is compulsory in Dutch primary and secondary schools?
cards.back: Sexuality and sexual diversity.

cards.front: Until what age are parents legally liable for their child's acts?
cards.back: Until the child turns 16.

cards.front: What do Dutch schools expect of parents?
cards.back: Involvement in their child's development at school.

cards.front: Name the two ways parents are involved at school.
cards.back: Scheduled parent-teacher meetings, and voluntary help with school activities.

cards.front: Name four sources of help with upbringing problems.
cards.back: The gemeente, jeugdzorg, the huisarts, and the school.

cards.front: When does the kinderbescherming take a case to a judge?
cards.back: Only on serious signals.

cards.front: Name four costs associated with education in NL.
cards.back: School fees, the parental contribution, learning materials, and travel costs.

cards.front: What is the status of the ouderbijdrage?
cards.back: Voluntary.

cards.front: Where can you apply for reduction or waiver of school costs?
cards.back: At the school itself, and through gemeente minimaregelingen.

cards.front: Which body handles applications for study finance?
cards.back: DUO.
